regions.breakdown: 池袋 (Ikebukuro) is a major district in Tokyo. 戸田 (Toda) is a city in Saitama Prefecture. Both are destinations indicated by this highway sign.
首都高 (Shutoko) is an abbreviation for 首都高速道路 (Shuto Kōsoku Dōro), the Metropolitan Expressway network in and around Tokyo. 'SHUTO EXPWY' is the English abbreviation.

regions.original: 熊谷 春日部 岩槻
regions.breakdown: 熊谷 (Kumagaya), 春日部 (Kasukabe), and 岩槻 (Iwatsuki) are cities in Saitama Prefecture, serving as destinations.
東北道 (Tohoku-do) is an abbreviation for 東北自動車道 (Tohoku Jidōshadō), the Tohoku Expressway. 'E4' is its route number. 'TOHOKU EXPWY' is the English abbreviation.
Indicates the distance, in meters, to the respective exit or junction for the destinations listed above.
八王子 (Hachioji) is a city in Tokyo. 川越 (Kawagoe) is a city in Saitama Prefecture. Both are destinations indicated by this highway sign.
関越道 (Kan'etsu-do) is an abbreviation for 関越自動車道 (Kan'etsu Jidōshadō), the Kan-Etsu Expressway. 'E17' is its route number. 'KAN-ETSU EXP' is the English abbreviation.
Indicates the distance, in meters, to the respective exit or junction for the destinations listed above.

where_youd_see_it: On a highway in Japan, indicating directions to various cities and expressways.
cultural_note: Japanese highway signs often include both Japanese kanji/kana and romaji (romanized Japanese), along with English translations of expressway names, to assist international drivers. Common expressway names like '首都高' (Shutoko), '東北道' (Tohoku-do), and '関越道' (Kan-Etsu-do) are frequently abbreviated on signs.
